record.paper_title: An unsolved problem on the powers of 3/2
record.original_question: For sequences alpha times (3/2)^n with alpha a positive real number and n = 0, 1, 2, ..., can a theory analogous to the theory developed by Mahler for fractional parts lying in [0, 1/2) be established when the fractional parts are required to lie in subintervals of [0, 1) whose length is smaller than 1/2, possibly even arbitrarily small?

evidence.quote: It would be very interesting if a similar theory could be established for subintervals of smaller length, or perhaps even of arbitrarily small length.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a positive real number $\alpha$ and a nonnegative integer $n$, let $\{\alpha(3/2)^n\}$ denote the fractional part of $\alpha(3/2)^n$. It is known (after Mahler) that one can develop a substantive theory describing the set of $\alpha>0$ for which $\{\alpha(3/2)^n\}\in[0,1/2)$ holds for every $n=0,1,2,\dots$ (so-called $Z$-numbers); in particular, the set of such $\alpha$ in any interval $[N,N+1)$ with $N$ a positive integer is finite, and quantitative bounds on its cardinality are available.

Develop an analogous theory in which the target interval $[0,1/2)$ is replaced by a subinterval $I\subset[0,1)$ of length $\ell<1/2$, and in particular for $\ell$ arbitrarily small. That is, for an interval $I\subset[0,1)$ with $|I|<1/2$, study the set
$$S_I=\{\alpha>0:\{\alpha(3/2)^n\}\in I\text{ for all }n=0,1,2,\dots\},$$
and establish structural and quantitative results (finiteness in bounded intervals, density bounds, existence/non-existence statements) parallel to those known in the case $I=[0,1/2)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem (Mahler's 3/2 problem) remains open, and even the existence of Z-numbers is unresolved. However, partial analogues for smaller target intervals have been established: Flatto–Lagarias–Pollington proved that for any real ξ≠0 and coprime integers p>q>1, the fractional parts {ξ(p/q)^n} cannot all lie in an interval of length strictly less than 1/p (giving 1/3 for 3/2); Dubickas and others have sharpened these results, exhibiting forbidden subintervals and quantitative bounds. A fully analogous theory for arbitrarily small intervals is not established.

status_evidence.title: Mahler's 3/2 problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Mahler conjectured in 1968 that there are no Z-numbers... the problem remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The original 3/2 problem is still open.

status_evidence.title: On the fractional parts of rational powers (Dubickas)
status_evidence.snippet: For any real ξ≠0 and coprime integers p>q>1, the fractional parts {ξ(p/q)^n} cannot all lie in an interval of length strictly smaller than 1/p.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for smaller target intervals, giving the threshold 1/p.

status_evidence.title: Mahler's 3/2 problem in Z+
status_evidence.snippet: Recent progress restricting limit sets of {λ(3/2)^n} to explicit subintervals.
status_evidence.claim: Refinements regarding smaller subintervals continue to appear.
